mainTopic: How many people are called to the תורה, what the numbers stand for, and who counts toward the seven
overview: The amud opens by finishing the earlier discussion about bowing: like אביי, רבא only bent over and did not lie flat on the ground. The גמרא then asks who wrote the משנה that gives five readers on יום טוב, six on יום הכפורים, and seven on שבת, with adding allowed. A ברייתא shows that this fits neither רבי ישמעאל nor רבי עקיבא. רבא answers that it follows the version of רבי ישמעאל taught in his school, and the גמרא explains that two תנאים reported רבי ישמעאל's view differently. Next the גמרא discusses what the numbers 3, 5 and 7 stand for: either the word counts of ברכת כהנים or the king's officials named in the verses, which רב יוסף's ברייתא supports. The six readers of יום הכפורים match the six people who stood on each side of עזרא, with זכריה and משולם being one man. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that anyone, even a קטן or a woman, counts toward the seven, though a woman should not read because of כבוד ציבור. The גמרא then asks whether the מפטיר counts as one of the seven, and it starts to defend the view that he does not, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא only bent over instead of fully lying down
steps.stepSummary: This is the closing line of the previous discussion about bowing. רבא would only tilt or bend his body and did not fully stretch out on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא, who would only bend over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the earlier discussion about falling on one's face during תפילה by describing what רבא used to do. It is the tail end of the earlier topic, not part of the new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud the גמרא discussed full prostration (פישוט ידים ורגלים) during נפילת אפים. This line finishes a sentence that began there and named אביי together with רבא. It describes the practice they followed instead: tilting or bending to the side rather than lying flat.

keyTerms.meaning: would merely bend or tilt over, without fully lying down
full prostration with arms and legs stretched out (the background concept)

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the previous sugya about bowing. Do not try to connect it to the משנה about Torah readers that comes next.

phrases.english: and Rava, who would merely bend over.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the earlier discussion about bowing all the way down.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא דִּמְצַלֵּי אַצְלוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous sugya (from the prior daf) about bowing during תפילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא only bent over, so full prostration never came up for him.

steps.title: The משנה's numbers of Torah readers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: five people are called up on יום טוב and six on יום הכפורים (and, as the משנה continues, seven on שבת, with permission to add).
steps.simpleTranslation: On יום טוב, five; on יום הכפורים, six; and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה it is about to analyze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה lists five readers on יום טוב, six on יום הכפורים, and seven on שבת. It also says you may not go below these numbers but you may add to them. Both details, the exact numbers and the permission to add, will matter in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: 'etc.', meaning the rest of the quoted text continues

phrases.english: On a Festival, five,
on Yom Kippur, six, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: on שבת seven; one may not decrease but may add.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּיוֹם טוֹב חֲמִשָּׁה, בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שִׁשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new sugya, unrelated to the bowing discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five readers on יום טוב, six on יום הכפורים, seven on שבת. One may not go below these numbers but may add.

steps.title: Who is the author of the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the משנה and claims it matches neither רבי ישמעאל nor רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the author of our משנה? It is neither רבי ישמעאל nor רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows and makes a surprising claim: it seems to match no known view. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a משנה follows some known תנא. Saying it matches neither main view creates a puzzle that the גמרא now has to justify and then solve.

keyTerms.meaning: who is it? (asking which תנא is the author)

phrases.english: Our Mishnah, who is its author?

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְלָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: It is not Rabbi Yishmael and not Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who authored the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view does the משנה follow?

steps.title: The ברייתא with both views
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the two views. רבי ישמעאל says 5-6-7 with no adding. רבי עקיבא says 5-7-6 with adding allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: On יום טוב five, on יום הכפורים six, on שבת seven; one may not decrease or add. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: On יום טוב five, on יום הכפורים seven, on שבת six; one may not decrease but may add.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove why the משנה fits neither תנא. It lays out each view so the mismatch can be seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל has the same numbers as the משנה, but he forbids adding. רבי עקיבא allows adding like the משנה, but he gives יום הכפורים seven and שבת six, the reverse of the משנה. Each one matches the משנה on one point and differs on the other.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the numbers carefully. רבי עקיבא does not change the total. He swaps them: seven on יום הכפורים and six on שבת.

phrases.english: As it was taught: On a Festival, five,
and on Yom Kippur, six, and on Shabbat, seven;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: one may not decrease from them and one may not add to them,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: בְּיוֹם טוֹב חֲמִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: On a Festival, five,
and on Yom Kippur, seven, and on Shabbat, six;
phrases.notes: The reverse of the משנה's numbers.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן אֲבָל מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן.
phrases.english: one may not decrease from them, but one may add to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim that the משנה follows neither תנא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה matches neither רבי ישמעאל nor רבי עקיבא

steps.title: Spelling out why neither תנא fits
steps.stepSummary: If the author is רבי ישמעאל, the permission to add is a problem. If it is רבי עקיבא, the numbers six and seven are a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is it? If רבי ישמעאל, the adding is difficult! If רבי עקיבא, six and seven are difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its question and lays out exactly where each option fails. This sharpens the problem before the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל fails on the rule (adding is forbidden in his view). רבי עקיבא fails on the numbers (he swaps יום הכפורים and שבת). Every known view conflicts with the משנה on some point.

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? אִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל — קַשְׁיָא תּוֹסֶפֶת!
phrases.english: Who is it? If Rabbi Yishmael, the adding is difficult!

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא — קַשְׁיָא שִׁשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעָה!
phrases.english: If Rabbi Akiva, the six and seven are difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל — קַשְׁיָא תּוֹסֶפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא to state exactly how each option conflicts with the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Attributing the משנה to either רבי ישמעאל or רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל forbids adding, but the משנה allows it. רבי עקיבא reverses six and seven compared to the משנה.

steps.title: רבא: It follows the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה follows the version taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל. That version has 5-6-7 and also allows adding, matching the משנה exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל. For the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: On יום טוב five, on יום הכפורים six, on שבת seven; one may not decrease but may add. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the puzzle by pointing to a different tradition of רבי ישמעאל's view. In that version, רבי ישמעאל agrees with every detail of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two reports of רבי ישמעאל's opinion. The first ברייתא says he forbids adding. The ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל says he allows adding. Since the second version has both the משנה's numbers and its permission to add, the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל as reported by his school.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא taught in the study hall (school) of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (5 on יום טוב, 6 on יום הכפורים, 7 on שבת, adding allowed) follows רבי ישמעאל as reported by his own school, not as reported in the first ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא settles authorship. When a תנא's view is reported in two different ways, one of those reports can fit the משנה perfectly.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: תְּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא.
phrases.english: Rava said: It is the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael.
For the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב חֲמִשָּׁה, בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שִׁשָּׁה,
phrases.english: On a Festival, five; on Yom Kippur, six;
on Shabbat, seven;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן אֲבָל מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: one may not decrease from them, but one may add to them,
phrases.notes: Unlike the first ברייתא's version of רבי ישמעאל, adding is allowed here.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: תְּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternate tradition of a תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל forbids adding, so the משנה cannot be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to the tradition of his school, רבי ישמעאל allows adding, so the משנה follows him.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל's school, which allows adding, it clashes with the first ברייתא, where רבי ישמעאל forbids adding.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between one statement of רבי ישמעאל and another statement of רבי ישמעאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a new problem created by רבא's answer: we now have two versions of רבי ישמעאל that disagree with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, רבי ישמעאל says you may not add people. In the version from רבי ישמעאל's school, adding is allowed. One person cannot hold both positions.

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: Rabbi Yishmael's statement
against Rabbi Yishmael's statement!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אַדְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a side effect of רבא's answer in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The two reports of רבי ישמעאל's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא has רבי ישמעאל forbidding additions. The school's version has him allowing them. These cannot both be his view.

steps.title: Two תנאים reported רבי ישמעאל differently
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction comes from two students who each transmitted רבי ישמעאל's view differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two תנאים disagree about what רבי ישמעאל held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל did not contradict himself. Two later תנאים simply reported his opinion differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is about the transmission of the view, not inside רבי ישמעאל's own thinking. One report forbids adding, and the other, which our משנה follows, allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים (two transmitters of a teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows one report of רבי ישמעאל's view: 5-6-7, with adding allowed. Another report of his view forbids adding.

phrases.english: Two tannaim (disagree)
about the view of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two transmitters disagree about one master's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל himself holds two opposite positions
steps.terutzMaskana: Two students reported his view differently, so there is no self-contradiction

steps.title: Who taught the ברייתא about arriving and leaving?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about how early people come to and leave בית הכנסת on יום טוב, יום הכפורים and שבת, and asks who its author is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught this ברייתא? On יום טוב people come late and leave early. On יום הכפורים they come early and leave late. On שבת they come early and leave early.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a related question: which תנא wrote this ברייתא about service timing. It is setting up a suggested answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב people are busy cooking, so they come late, and they leave early to eat. On שבת the food is already cooked, so they come early, but they still leave early to eat. The unusual case is יום הכפורים, where people stay late, and the גמרא wants to know whose view explains that.

keyTerms.meaning: They hurry, come or go early

phrases.english: Who taught this that was taught in a baraita:
On a Festival, people are late to arrive,
and quick to leave.
On Yom Kippur, they are quick to arrive,
and late to leave.
And on Shabbat, they are quick to arrive,
and quick to leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא לְהָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related question built on the ברייתא of step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The author of the ברייתא about arrival and departure times

steps.title: Suggestion: it is רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי עקיבא, who has an extra person read on יום הכפורים, which makes the service longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say it is רבי עקיבא, who holds that there is an extra man called up (on יום הכפורים)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes an answer: רבי עקיבא. He has seven people read on יום הכפורים, so the reading takes longer and people leave late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, יום הכפורים gets seven readers, more than שבת's six. That extra reader would explain why people stay late on יום הכפורים.
steps.confusionAlert: "לימא" is only a suggestion. It often gets rejected right away, as happens in the next step.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is Rabbi Akiva,
who holds there is an extra man (reading on Yom Kippur)?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a tentative answer to the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא, because his extra reader lengthens the יום הכפורים service

steps.title: Even רבי ישמעאל fits, because the prayers are long
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is pushed aside: people leave late on יום הכפורים because the day's prayers are long, so רבי ישמעאל fits too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it is רבי ישמעאל, because the order of prayers of the day is long.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for רבי עקיבא. The late ending does not have to come from an extra reader. It can come from the long יום הכפורים prayers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step removes the need for רבי עקיבא. The ברייתא's timing is explained by the long תפילות, with all the requests and confessions. So the ברייתא does not show who its author is.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the day's prayers

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Yishmael —
because the order (of prayers) of the day is long.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא must follow רבי עקיבא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Leaving late can be explained by the long prayers, not only by an extra reader

steps.title: What do the numbers 3, 5 and 7 stand for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the numbers of people called to the תורה correspond to: 3 on weekdays, 5 on יום טוב and 7 on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: These numbers, three, five and seven, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the source or symbolism of the numbers 3, 5 and 7. It is setting up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three people are called on Monday, Thursday and שבת afternoon, five on יום טוב, and seven on שבת. The גמרא wants to know what pattern these numbers reflect.

phrases.english: These three, five and seven
correspond to what?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲמִשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעָה כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the numbers in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the numbers 3, 5 and 7 correspond to

steps.title: Two answers: ברכת כהנים or the king's officers
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים (whose exact names are reported in different ways) disagree. One says the numbers match the word counts of ברכת כהנים. The other says they match the king's guards and advisers named in the verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר נחמני and one other scholar disagree about this, namely רבי שמעון בן פזי. Some say it was רבי שמעון בן פזי and one other scholar, namely רבי יצחק בר נחמני, and some say רבי שמואל בר נחמני. One said: it corresponds to ברכת כהנים. The other said: it corresponds to the three guards of the door, the five who saw the king's face, and the seven who saw the king's face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a dispute. First it lists the different reports of who the disputants were, then it gives the two explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three verses of ברכת כהנים have 3, 5 and 7 Hebrew words. The other view points to verses about royal officials: 3 guards of the door and 5 who saw the king's face (מלכים ב כ״ה), and 7 who saw the king's face (אסתר א׳). Each view gives the numbers a meaningful source.

keyTerms.meaning: And one other scholar with him

steps.confusionAlert: The long list of names only records which scholars took part. Don't get lost in it. The key point is the two explanations at the end.

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani disagrees about this
with one (scholar) who was with him,
and who is he? Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
phrases.english: And some say: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi
and one (scholar) who was with him,
and who is he? Rabbi Yitzchak bar Nachmani,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי.
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani.
One said: corresponding to the Priestly Blessing,
phrases.notes: Its three verses have 3, 5 and 7 words

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד שְׁלֹשָׁה שׁוֹמְרֵי הַסַּף,
phrases.english: and one said: corresponding to the three guards of the door,
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק in II Kings 25:18.

phrases.english: five of those who saw the king's face,
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק in II Kings 25:19.

phrases.english: seven who saw the king's face.
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק in Esther 1:14.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי וְחַד דְּעַמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with a dispute
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the word counts of ברכת כהנים, or the numbers of royal officials in the verses

steps.title: רב יוסף's ברייתא supports the royal officers view
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף taught a ברייתא matching 3, 5 and 7 to the guards and the king's advisers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: three, five and seven are the three guards of the door, five of those who saw the king's face, and seven who saw the king's face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the second opinion in the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second view is not just a guess by an אמורא. A ברייתא taught by רב יוסף says the same thing, which gives that view earlier support.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who see the king's face (top royal advisers)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught (a baraita):
Three, five and seven —
three guards of the door,
five of those who saw the king's face,
seven who saw the king's face.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second opinion of step 13
steps.raayaObject: The view that 3-5-7 match the royal officials
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רב יוסף

steps.title: אביי asks why רב יוסף never explained this before
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks his teacher רב יוסף why he had not taught them this explanation until now.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Why has the Master not explained this to us until now?
steps.whatsHappening: A short story follows. אביי, רב יוסף's student, asks why he is only hearing this now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a legal challenge. It is a personal exchange between student and teacher. It shows that the ברייתא was new to אביי.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Until now, what is the reason
that the Master did not explain it to us?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי עַד הָאִידָּנָא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא פָּרִישׁ לַן מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רב יוסף's ברייתא from step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב יוסף had not taught this explanation earlier

steps.title: רב יוסף: I did not know you needed it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that he did not know they needed it, and that he has never refused to answer a question.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not know that you needed it. Have you ever asked me something and I did not tell you?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי. He assumed they already knew it, and he reminds אביי that he always answers when asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer shows that a teacher may not offer every piece of information on his own. The student needs to ask. This closes the discussion about 3, 5 and 7.
steps.whatToRemember: The numbers 3, 5 and 7 of the people called to the תורה match either the word counts of ברכת כהנים or the royal officials in the verses. רב יוסף's ברייתא supports the second view.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I did not know that you needed it,
and did you ever ask me something
and I did not tell you?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לָא הֲוָה יָדַעְנָא דִּצְרִיכִיתוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question in step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He did not realize they needed it, and he always answers when asked

steps.title: What do the six readers of יום הכפורים match?
steps.stepSummary: יעקב מינאה asks רב יהודה what the six readers on יום הכיפורים correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: יעקב מינאה said to רב יהודה: These six people called up on יום הכיפורים, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone asks the same kind of question as before, but now about the six readers on יום הכיפורים, which was not covered by the 3-5-7 discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps explained 3, 5 and 7. יום הכיפורים has its own number, six, so it needs its own explanation. The question sets up a fresh source for that number.

keyTerms.meaning: יעקב of Mina (some read it as 'the sectarian'), who put the question to רב יהודה
The day when six people are called to the תורה
Corresponding to whom? What do they match?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ יַעֲקֹב מִינָאָה לְרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Yaakov of Mina said to Rav Yehuda:
These six readers of Yom Kippur
what do they correspond to?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי שִׁשָּׁה דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'what does the number correspond to' question from step 12 to the number on יום הכיפורים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or symbolism behind having six readers on יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: The six match the people standing beside Ezra
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that six matches the six people who stood on each side of עזרא when he read the תורה, quoting נחמיה 8:4.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: They match the six who stood on עזרא's right and the six on his left, as the verse says: 'עזרא the scribe stood on a wooden platform made for this purpose, and next to him stood מתתיה, שמע, ענייה, אוריה, חלקיה and מעשיה on his right, and on his left פדיה, מישאל, מלכיה, חשום, חשבדנה, זכריה, משולם.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the answer: the number six comes from the public תורה reading of עזרא, where six people stood on each side of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא's reading was the model public reading of the תורה, so it makes sense to tie a reading number to it. The proof is the list of names in the verse. That list is about to cause a problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: עזרא the scribe, who led the public תורה reading in נחמיה
On his right / on his left

phrases.english: He said to him: Corresponding to the six
who stood at Ezra's right
and the six at his left,
as it is said: 'And Ezra the scribe stood'
upon a wooden platform
which they had made for the purpose
and beside him stood Mattithiah and Shema

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲנָיָה וְאוּרִיָּה וְחִלְקִיָּה וּמַעֲשֵׂיָה עַל יְמִינוֹ
phrases.english: and Anaiah and Uriah and Hilkiah and Maaseiah on his right
and on his left Pedaiah and Mishael and Malchiah
and Hashum and Hashbadanah, Zechariah, Meshullam.'
phrases.notes: Count the left side: this looks like seven names, which sets up the next question.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּנֶגֶד שִׁשָּׁה שֶׁעָמְדוּ מִימִינוֹ שֶׁל עֶזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The six readers match the six people on each side of עזרא at his public תורה reading (נחמיה 8:4).

steps.title: But the left side has seven names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the verse lists seven people on עזרא's left, not six.
steps.simpleTranslation: But those are seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא counts the names on the left side of the verse and finds seven, which seems to break רב יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on exactly six on each side. If the left side has seven, the verse does not match the number six. This is a direct challenge to the proof text.

phrases.english: These are seven!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי שִׁבְעָה הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the verse quoted in step 18 as proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that six people stood on עזרא's left.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting the names in the verse gives seven on the left: פדיה, מישאל, מלכיה, חשום, חשבדנה, זכריה, משולם.

steps.title: זכריה and משולם are one person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that זכריה and משולם are two names for the same man. He was called משולם because his deeds were perfect.
steps.simpleTranslation: זכריה is the same person as משולם. Why was he called משולם? Because he was perfect (משלם) in his deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the count: the last two names belong to one person, so there really are only six on the left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once two names are joined into one person, the left side has six people, matching the right side. The גמרא also explains the second name: 'משולם' sounds like 'perfect', a title for his good deeds. This saves רב יהודה's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as; identical to

phrases.english: Zechariah is the same as Meshullam,
and why was he called Meshullam?
Because he was perfect in his deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ זְכַרְיָה הַיְינוּ מְשֻׁלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the counting problem raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the verse: two names refer to one person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: זכריה and משולם are two separate people, making seven on the left.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are one person with a second name, so there are six on each side and the number six for יום הכיפורים stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The six readers on יום הכיפורים match the six people on each side of עזרא. זכריה and משולם are one man, called משולם because his deeds were perfect.

steps.title: Anyone counts toward the seven, but a woman should not read
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that everyone counts toward the seven readers, even a קטן and a woman. But the חכמים said a woman should not read because of כבוד ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Everyone counts toward the seven readers, even a minor and even a woman. But the חכמים said: A woman should not read in the תורה, because of the honor of the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: who may be counted as one of the seven people called to the תורה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first gives the basic rule that a קטן or a woman can count among the seven. Then it adds a limit: the חכמים said a woman should not actually read, because of כבוד ציבור. The basic permission stays, but a separate concern means it is not carried out in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Count toward the quorum of seven readers
A minor (a child below בר מצוה)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say a woman is excluded from the category of people who can count. It says she can count, and then adds that she should not read because of כבוד ציבור.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּל עוֹלִין לַמִּנְיָן שִׁבְעָה,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: All count toward the quorum of seven,
even a minor and even a woman.
But the Sages said:
A woman should not read in the Torah,
because of the honor of the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַכֹּל עוֹלִין לַמִּנְיָן שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why the numbers exist to who may fill those numbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone, even a קטן or a woman, counts toward the seven readers, but a woman should not read because of כבוד ציבור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the question of who fills the seven places, which leads directly to the next question about the מפטיר.

steps.title: Does the מפטיר count as one of the seven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the מפטיר counts toward the seven required readers.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: The מפטיר, does he count toward the seven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question about the seven readers: does the person who reads the הפטרה count as one of them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מפטיר reads a short part of the תורה, then reads the הפטרה from the נביאים. The question is whether his תורה reading makes him one of the seven, or whether his job is mainly the הפטרה so he is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
The one who concludes and reads the הפטרה

steps.confusionAlert: The מפטיר does read from the תורה too, before the הפטרה. That is exactly why there is a question.

phrases.english: It was asked of them: the maftir,
what is the law, does he count toward the seven?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַפְטִיר, מַהוּ שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה לַמִּנְיָן שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of who counts toward the seven, now about the מפטיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the מפטיר is counted as one of the seven שבת readers.

steps.title: רב הונא and רבי ירמיה בר אבא disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רבי ירמיה בר אבא disagree: one says the מפטיר counts, and one says he does not. The one who says he counts reasons that he does read from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רבי ירמיה בר אבא: one said he counts, and one said he does not count. The one who said he counts: because he does read from the תורה,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records a dispute about the מפטיר and starts to explain each side, beginning with the view that he counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view that he counts looks at what the מפטיר actually does: he reads from the תורה like the others, so he should count. The reason for the other view is given in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba:
one said: he counts,
and one said: he does not count.
The one who said he counts —
because he does read,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues next with the reasoning of the other side.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא, חַד אָמַר: עוֹלֶה, וְחַד אָמַר: אֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 with two opposing opinions, then starts to explain the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a dispute. One view says the מפטיר counts because he reads from the תורה. The other says he does not count, and its reason is given in step 24.

steps.title: Why one opinion says the מפטיר does not count
steps.stepSummary: The view that the מפטיר does not count follows עולא. עולא says the מפטיר reads from the תורה only out of כבוד תורה, so he is not part of the seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says the מפטיר does not count holds like עולא. עולא said: Why must the person who reads the הפטרה first read from the תורה? Because of כבוד תורה. And since his תורה reading is only for כבוד תורה, he is not counted in the number of seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the reasoning of the second opinion from the last step, the one who says the מפטיר does not count toward the seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא explains why the הפטרה reader must read from the תורה first. If he read only the נביא, people might think the נביא is as important as the תורה. So his תורה reading is only there to protect the honor of the תורה. It is not a real part of the required seven עליות, so he does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who concludes with a reading from the Prophets (the הפטרה reader)
He does not count toward the number

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the מפטיר's עליה as an 'honor' עליה rather than a required one. That is why, in practice, the מפטיר is seen as an addition to the required number of readers.

phrases.english: And the one who said he does not count holds like Ulla.
As Ulla said:
For what reason does the one who concludes with the Prophets
need to read from the Torah first?
Because of respect for the Torah.
phrases.notes: Otherwise people might think the Prophets and the Torah have equal honor.

phrases.english: And since it is only because of respect for the Torah,
he does not count toward the number (of seven).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵינוֹ עוֹלֶה כִּדְעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the מחלוקת from step 23 by giving the reason for the second opinion
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מפטיר does not count, because his תורה reading is only for כבוד תורה (עולא).

steps.title: The 21-verse הפטרה seems to show the מפטיר is one of the seven
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the הפטרה must be at least 21 verses, matching the seven תורה readers (7 × 3). If the מפטיר were an extra eighth reader, the number should be 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: The one who reads the הפטרה should not read fewer than twenty-one verses, matching the seven who read in the תורה. And if it is true that the מפטיר is an extra reader, it should be twenty-four!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the opinion that the מפטיר does not count, using a ברייתא about how long the הפטרה must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תורה reader must read at least three verses, so seven readers read at least 21 verses. The ברייתא matches the הפטרה to 21, which means it counts only seven readers in total, including the מפטיר. If the מפטיר were an eighth reader, there would be eight readers and at least 24 verses, so the הפטרה should be 24.

keyTerms.meaning: He should not do less than
And if it is so (if your claim were true)

steps.confusionAlert: The numbers come from the rule that each עליה is at least 3 verses: 7 readers × 3 = 21, but 8 readers × 3 = 24. The 21 refers to the minimum total read in the תורה, which the הפטרה is meant to match.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The one who concludes with the Prophets may not read fewer
than twenty-one verses,
corresponding to the seven who read in the Torah.
And if it is so (that the מפטיר is an extra reader),
it would be twenty-four!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי הַמַּפְטִיר בְּנָבִיא לֹא יִפְחוֹת מֵעֶשְׂרִים וְאֶחָד פְּסוּקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion explained in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The view (עולא) that the מפטיר does not count toward the seven
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא matches the הפטרה to seven readers × 3 verses = 21. If the מפטיר were an eighth reader, it should be 8 × 3 = 24.

steps.title: Starting the answer: it is only for כבוד תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer by repeating that the מפטיר's reading is only for כבוד תורה. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since his reading is only because of כבוד תורה —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer to the challenge about 21 vs. 24. The sentence continues on the next amud, so this line sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer goes back to עולא's idea: the מפטיר's תורה reading is only an honor, not a real required עליה. So it makes sense that the 21-verse count leaves him out and counts only the seven real readers. The full wording of this answer comes next.

phrases.english: Since it is only because of respect for the Torah —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּמִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹד תּוֹרָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reapplying the original reasoning (the reading is only for כבוד תורה) to explain the count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 21 verses seem to show that the מפטיר is one of the seven readers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the מפטיר's תורה reading is only for honor, the count of 21 is based on the seven real readers only (completed on the next amud).
